correctness.rationale: By SU(2) Peter-Weyl characters, highest-weight cutoff S_L is convolution with K_L(theta)=sum_{m=1}^{M}m sin(m theta)/sin theta, M=L+1. Haar probability Weyl density 2/pi sin² theta makes endpoint L1 and Linfty operator norms equal (2/pi)∫0^pi |sum m sin(m theta)|sin theta dtheta. Algebraic identity sin theta sum m sin(m theta)=-M cos(theta/2)cos((M+1/2)theta)+(1/2)cot(theta/2)sin(M theta) was independently checked with maximal sampled error 1.8e-12. Its second term integrates O(log M) by splitting at 1/M, cot(theta/2)≤2/theta and sin(M theta)≤M theta near zero. The absolute cosine Fourier expansion has mean 2/pi and summable k^-2 coefficients; integration by parts gives weighted integral ∫cos(theta/2)|cos((M+1/2)theta)|=4/pi+O(1/M). Hence norm=(8/pi²)M+O(log M). Independent midpoint integrations M=32,128,512 gave norm/M .8198525004,.8129236562,.8111618525 approaching 8/pi²=.8105694691; asymptotic is proved analytically, not by numerics.
